definitions: A doctrine of military strategy and national security policy in which a full-scale use of nuclear weapons by two or more opposing sides would cause the complete annihilation of both the attacker and the defender.
The idea that the threat of nuclear retaliation prevents either side from launching a first strike.
examples: The Cold War was largely defined by the concept of mutually assured destruction.
Many strategists believe that mutually assured destruction prevented a direct conflict between superpowers.
The principle of mutually assured destruction relies on both parties having second-strike capabilities.
